The infamous car scene in The Haunting of Hill House is absolute pinnacle of horror direction because of its devastating misdirection. By locking the audience into a deeply tense, realistic argument between Shirley and Theo, director Mike Flanagan weaponizes human emotion to lower your guard before delivering a shattering shock by breaking Nell  through the frame.

What makes The Haunting of Hill House legendary is that the house isn't just a spooky backdrop, but a sentient, malevolent entity that preys on the psychological isolation and suppressed desires of its inhabitants. Whether you explore the chilling 1959 gothic classic by Shirley Jackson or the emotionally devastating 2018 television series on Netflix, both masterpieces use the architecture of terror to ask whether the ghosts are actually outside us, or if we are the ones haunted by ourselves.
